subject: Serving congestion: scoped exception request + customer notice draft
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: SRE Team <sre@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: [ALERT] Regional serving congestion — initial triage and ask

Folks —

We started seeing a sustained increase in tail latency for the gen-api in us-west-2 around 08:45 PDT. P95 across several fleet pools jumped from ~210ms to ~1.2s; throughput per instance dropped ~25% despite normal qps. Initial SRE triage shows an instance-class imbalance; one node group is hitting NVMe IO stalls intermittently. I'm attaching a short service graph (service-graph.png).

Immediate asks:
- SRE: confirm whether we should scale the node group or drain the affected instances (Markus, Marissa please coordinate).
- Product: we need a short, customer-facing note outlining impact and next steps; can someone draft? (Grace / Jonas)
- Engineering: is there a short-term config we can flip (instance-level IO backlog limits, aggressive backoff) that won't require a full rollout? If so, we should push a scoped exception.

I think the correct path is targeted instance drainage + a temporary routing exception to avoid the affected AZ while we confirm root cause. We should avoid a global routing change.

Markus
Senior SRE Liaison
Redwood Inference

Attachments: service-graph.png
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Cc: SRE Ops <sre@redwood.com>, Eng Infra <infra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-28T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] Regional serving congestion — initial triage and ask

On 2026-05-28 09:12, Markus Klein wrote:
> Immediate asks:
> - SRE: confirm whether we should scale the node group or drain the affected instances (Markus, Marissa please coordinate).

Marking next steps from infra side:
1) I kicked a controlled drain of the three flagged instances in ng-usw2-highmem-7 at 09:30; replacement instances are healthy but we are seeing the congestion reappear after ~20m on the replacement set.
2) Stack traces point to intermittent NVMe IO queue growth on the underlying host (we're coordinating with cloud infra).
3) Short-term mitigations we can flip via runtime flags (no deploy): enable aggressive token-batching backpressure (runtime flag: enable_adaptive_backpressure=true) and tighten IO timeouts to fail-fast (io_timeout_ms=1200). These are config flags that don't require a model rollout but do require a minor restart of the serving worker process (rolling, per-pool).

Impact tradeoffs: tighter IO timeouts will increase immediate error-surface for long requests, but will prevent classic queue head-of-line blocking that amplifies tail latency. I recommend applying the flags to the affected node group only and keeping an aggressive watch for error rate increase.

Action: Markus / SRE can you authorize a scoped exception to apply these runtime flags and do a rolling restart limited to ng-usw2-highmem-7? If approved, I'll schedule the roll and a canary.

- Marissa

Attachments: (none)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-05-28T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Orbit Labs — brief notice: transient increased latency in us-west-2 (draft)

Aisha —

I wanted to flag that our telemetry detected a transient increase in latency for some generation calls originating in the us-west-2 region this morning. Our SRE team has identified an IO-related imbalance in a small subset of nodes and is performing targeted mitigations.

What we're doing now:
- Isolating affected instances and draining traffic away from the small subset of hosts.
- Applying a short-lived, targeted runtime configuration to reduce queuing amplification (no model changes).
- Monitoring and will follow up with any customer-facing escalation if we see error rates rise.

Expected customer impact:
- Brief increase in P95 for requests routed to the affected hosts between ~08:45–09:45 PDT; most traffic was unaffected.

Next update: We'll provide a follow-up note by 15:00 PDT with the remediation status and any confirmed mitigation steps. If you'd like a post-incident summary (root cause + timeline), we can schedule that for this week.

Grace O'Connor
Head of Customer Ops
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-05-28T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: [ALERT] Regional serving congestion — scoped exception applied, customer update sent

Quick update after the scoped rollout: we applied the runtime flags (enable_adaptive_backpressure=true, io_timeout_ms=1200) to ng-usw2-highmem-7 at 12:10 PDT with a controlled rolling restart. Canary looked clean (5m window) and we continued roll to remaining instances in the node group.

Observations:
- P95 returned to ~230ms on the node group after the roll.
- Error rate briefly increased by 0.6% absolute during the canary; we rolled with a narrow blast radius and watched for user-visible errors.
- Cloud provider acknowledged an NVMe host-level degradation and marked a small set of hosts for replacement.

Next steps / asks:
- Product (Grace / Jonas): finalize the customer post by EOD and include an optional offer for a post-incident readout if Orbit wants it.
- Infra/Eng: please follow up with the cloud team until the replacement hosts are verified; raise INF-9123 for any follow-up remediation tasks and quantization of risk for highmem pools.

Thanks everyone for the fast coordination. I'll post a short incident timeline and RCA link once the cloud replacement completes.

Markus
Senior SRE Liaison
Redwood Inference
